_comment: The ratio of valgebra to pydantic-core each shape must stay under: a claim the project makes, not a measurement it recorded. The argument for the ceilings, for the recorded block beside them and for the one shape excluded from it is docs/dev/07-tooling-ci.md, under 'The competitive ratio' -- a page the documentation lint reads and this file is not. Changing a ceiling or re-recording a ratio is an edit with an argument in its commit message; scripts/perf_gate.py --against is the fine-grained gate.
_free_threaded_comment: Ceilings the free-threaded build is held to instead, for the shapes where it is a different performance environment rather than the same one on a slower clock. A shape absent from here is held to the shared ceiling above. Reading an element out of a list takes the list's lock there, and a shape whose cost is per-element pays it; docs/11-performance.md measures that and says which shapes part.
_recorded_comment: The ratio each shape last measured, the spread it was measured across, and the environment both belong to. See docs/dev/07-tooling-ci.md for why a claim alone stopped being enough.

unratcheted.error_report: Not measurable on this instrument. Five runs of one PGO CPython 3.12 build read 0.861, 0.882, 0.889, 1.056 and 1.193 -- a spread of 0.33, a third of the shape's own value, where every other shape spreads between 0.001 and 0.048. A tolerance wide enough not to fire on that noise would be wider than any regression worth catching, and a tighter one would fire constantly. The shape keeps its ceiling of 1.60, which it is nowhere near crossing, and the reason it is noisy is worth its own reading: it is the only shape timing a path that raises and formats an exception, so a Python exception's cost is inside the measurement.

recorded._how_to_arm: Unrecorded on purpose: a recording made off the bench lane would match its fingerprint while carrying another machine's noise, so the first --update belongs on the lane, in a commit whose message carries the run. The tolerances are not waiting for that -- they are the shapes' own spread over twelve runs of one PGO CPython 3.12 build (scalar 0.008, large_array 0.004, deep_nesting 0.014, wide_record 0.029, json_document 0.057, build 0.001), each rounded up.
